extraction.summary: The test correlates a galaxy group's relative Hubble estimate from redshift and fundamental-plane distance with the fraction of its observer-to-group sightline inside finite-infinity regions. The central comparison is SDSS-based observations versus Millennium mocks for Lambda-CDM and a deliberately approximate timescape-inspired deformation of those same Lambda-CDM mocks. On the selected sample, the direct weighted-slope comparison strongly disfavors that imposed differential-expansion mock (9.50 sigma in the Local Group frame; 11.22 sigma in the CMB frame), while the binned-slope comparison is much weaker (1.52 and 2.08 sigma). KS and chi-square comparisons are poor/low-significance for both mock families, with an overall preference for Lambda-CDM. The tested alternative is not full timescape cosmology: it imposes a linear wall/void Hubble-rate relation on Millennium matter distributions with a softening factor of 0.75. The authors say their data show no significant support for timescape but do not fully exclude it or percent-level backreaction models.

ideas.title: Operational line-of-sight finite-infinity fraction
ideas.description: For each group, place 1000 equally spaced sample points along the straight observer-to-group line using the group's comoving fundamental-plane distance; f_fi is the fraction of sampled points lying inside one or more reconstructed spherical finite-infinity regions. Overlaps are counted as locations inside a region. The authors report less than 0.2% additional error against semi-analytic intersections for all observational sightlines. They explicitly distinguish this one-dimensional fraction from the three-dimensional timescape wall-volume fraction f_w0.
locators: HTML #S4.p1; PDF p.4 and p.7; Eq. (1) context

equations.expression: f_fi = N(sampled sightline locations inside finite-infinity regions) / 1000
equations.confidence: high; operational expression of the prose, not a displayed equation
equations.definitions: N counts locations inside the union of the reconstructed finite-infinity regions along the line from the origin observer to the group.
equations.domain: Sightlines to the selected local galaxy-group sample; f_fi is one-dimensional and is not equal to f_w0 except at limiting values 0 or 1.

ideas.title: Relative individual Hubble estimator from group redshift and FP distance
ideas.description: The group estimator is its median redshift divided by its comoving fundamental-plane distance, then normalized by the sample mean so the average relative Hubble parameter is unity. It is a relative diagnostic for the correlation test, not an absolute H0 measurement. Group redshifts and finite-infinity catalogues are evaluated in both CMB and Local Group rest frames.

equations.expression: H_i = z_group / D_FP; H_rel = H_i / mean_sample(H_i)
equations.locator: Section 4, PDF pp.4 and 6; prose definition
equations.confidence: high; normalization is stated in prose
equations.definitions: z_group is the group median redshift; D_FP is the comoving fundamental-plane distance. The source does not give a separate displayed equation for this estimator.
equations.domain: Observed and mock groups, with results expressed as dimensionless relative Hubble parameters.

ideas.title: Linear wall/void interpolation used to deform the Lambda-CDM mocks
ideas.description: Because no suitable self-consistent timescape simulation was available, the authors retain the Millennium late-time matter distribution and impose differential expansion through a linear relation between mean sightline finite-infinity fraction and wall, void, and dressed Hubble rates. They derive a void rate for each mock catalogue, rescale the Millennium H0=73 km s^-1 Mpc^-1 mocks to the quoted dressed value, modify relative group Hubble parameters using the dark-matter-based sightline fraction, and set b_soft=0.75. The full per-group deformation formula is not printed. The model assumes the matter distribution is a reasonable late-Universe proxy and does not model a self-consistent timescape peculiar-velocity field or screening.

equations.confidence: high; checked against HTML MathML annotation and rendered PDF
equations.definitions: f_fi is the average one-dimensional sightline fraction for a mock catalogue; H_0,w is the bare wall rate; H_0,v is the void rate; H_0,av is the dressed average rate.
equations.domain: An empirical linear interpolation used to calibrate this paper's toy deformation; it is not presented as the full timescape model equation. Authors state f_fi is not the 3D wall-volume fraction.

ideas.title: Coherent infall can mimic a differential-expansion trend
ideas.description: Infall toward clusters gives foreground galaxies higher redshift relative to distance than background galaxies because the overdense cluster lies in the latter sightlines. This produces a qualitatively similar redshift-space signal to the proposed timescape effect, so the authors include mock catalogues and morphology-sensitive selection to estimate it rather than treating a slope as unique evidence for differential expansion.
ideas.confidence: high for the stated confounder; this packet does not independently quantify it.

ideas.title: Selected-sample slope favors Lambda-CDM over the imposed differential-expansion mock
ideas.description: For groups with at least three early-type members and FP distance below 402.8 Mpc, the observed weighted slopes are -0.19 (Local Group) and -0.16 (CMB). Table 1 compares them with mean mock slopes -0.25 for Lambda-CDM and -0.39 for differential expansion. The authors' slope-based comparison places the differential-expansion mock 9.50 and 11.22 standard deviations from the observed slopes, respectively. This is a result against their approximate mock prescription, not a direct rejection of a fully specified timescape cosmology.
ideas.confidence: high for transcription of reported table values; significance interpretation is the authors' stated comparison.

ideas.title: Binned and distribution tests weaken a broad exclusion claim
ideas.description: For selected binned data, observed slopes are -0.24 (LG) and -0.20 (CMB); the differential-expansion mock slope is -0.34, giving 1.52 and 2.08 sigma differences, P=0.13 and 0.04, and two-model likelihoods 0.17 and 0.04. Most individual bins lie within both models' error bars. The authors report that KS probabilities are very low for both model families, although Lambda-CDM probabilities exceed the differential-expansion ones for all 36 paired mock sets; chi-square comparisons also favor Lambda-CDM overall but have low significance. They explicitly state current data/models do not fully exclude timescape.
ideas.confidence: high for reported values and authors' qualification.

caveats: The main alternative tested is an artificially deformed Lambda-CDM Millennium mock with a linear dependence on f_fi and b_soft=0.75. No complete timescape dynamics, screening, or self-consistent peculiar-motion field is simulated; the authors acknowledge this approximation and say a full timescape simulation would be preferable.

Finite-infinity regions are reconstructed bottom-up from observed groups although the theoretical construction is top-down. The reconstructed line fractions have about 15% scatter plus systematic shift against dark-matter truth; inferred FI sizes are uncertain by 15-20%.

The FP distance indicator has 10-20% statistical errors and residual systematics, including a richness-dependent distance/redshift trend not reproduced in the mocks. The Millennium mocks have too few rich groups, so the selected mock sample is disproportionately small (530-954 vs 1,835/1,844 observed groups).

The data cover about 22.7% of the sky, mostly the northern hemisphere; the sample misses the Local Void and Great Attractor region and includes Virgo, which can affect the peculiar-velocity field. CMB and LG rest frames differ only modestly in the final comparison.

The full-catalogue direct slope values are less discrepant than the selected-sample result; the binned slopes reduce the differential-model discrepancy to about 1.5-2.1 sigma. Individual bins generally overlap both models. KS probabilities are extremely low for both model families and chi-square tests have low significance, so these are comparative preferences rather than a clean absolute goodness-of-fit acceptance.
The likelihood column assumes only Lambda-CDM and this timescape-inspired approximation as possible options. Its relative likelihoods do not compare all cosmologies.
The source cites prior observational fits and simulation/catalogue papers, but those sources were not independently checked or read here.

usefulness.assessment: Useful as a test design and as a documented negative/qualified result for a particular differential-expansion signal: it defines a line-of-sight finite-infinity statistic, constructs matched mock catalogues, identifies coherent infall and selection/scatter limits, and reports a strong selected-slope discrepancy for its imposed toy signal. It is not a source for a fully specified or independently ruled-out timescape cosmology; any follow-up must preserve that lost scope and revisit the mock deformation, FP systematics, and survey-volume limitations.
